subject: DPA execution: clarify binding mechanism and DocuSign flow
messages:
From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@finserve.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Kaplan <alice.legal@finserve.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Initial: DPA redlines and transfer mechanism preference

Markus,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Attached are our preferred redlines to Redwood's standard DPA and a short note on cross-border transfer impact (FinServe-DPA-redlines.docx; transfers-impact-notes.pdf).

Two points we need to confirm before legal will sign:
- Binding mechanism for transfers to the US: we typically require either SCCs with a UK IDTA addendum for UK data, or a mutually-agreed transfer clause that provides equivalent safeguards.
- Subprocessor transparency: please confirm the current subprocessor list and whether Redwood is amenable to a 30-day notice period for additions with an opt-out right for high-risk subprocessors.

Can you loop in your legal and privacy team with a timeline for execution (we'd like to finish by the end of November)?

Regards,
Tom Reeves
Head of Legal Operations
FinServe Inc

P.S. We can receive the final DPA via DocuSign.
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@finserve.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA redlines and transfer mechanism preference

Tom — thanks for the materials, received and reviewing. Looping in Laura (privacy/legal) and Marissa (account lead) to confirm next steps.

Quick answers up front:
- We can support SCCs plus a UK IDTA addendum as an execution path; we also support certified Transfer Impact Assessments and a limited set of binding contractual terms where acceptable to both parties.
- Subprocessor notice: our standard is 30 days' notice for additions and a right to object for high-risk subprocessors; exceptions possible in emergency cases with retroactive notice.

Laura — can you take point on redline review and propose a set of counter-redlines that capture the SCCs+UK approach and the subprocessor language? Marissa — can you confirm the internal timeline; FinServe wants end-of-November sign-off.

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@finserve.com>; Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA redlines and transfer mechanism preference

Tom / Markus — thanks. I reviewed FinServe's redlines and prepared our proposed counter-redlines (attached: redwood_dpa_redlines_20261113.docx) and a short summary of acceptable transfer approaches (SCCs-UK-IDTA-summary.pdf). Key points: 

1) Binding mechanism: our recommended, lowest-friction path is the EU SCCs (2021) applied to covered processing plus a UK IDTA addendum where the DPA references UK personal data. We will:
   - Incorporate the SCCs by reference and include the standard modular language.
   - Add a UK IDTA addendum for UK-data processing; we will attach it as Annex B.
   - Add a narrow fallback clause that allows execution of an equivalent mechanism agreeable to both parties (i.e., documented BCR or alternative standard contractual clauses), but only with mutual written consent.

2) Subprocessors: we can accept a 30-day notice period for new subprocessors. For critical categories (KYC, payments, hosted data stores), we will offer a 15-day review window for objection with an escalation path to the Redwood Security team. If we object, we will propose reasonable mitigations (technical and contractual).

3) Audit and evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and summary transfer-impact materials. We'll produce a redacted SOC 2 report on request and the transfer-impact summary as part of the DPA folder.

4) Execution: we can do DocuSign. Our preference is to keep execution synchronous (single envelope including DPA and UK addendum). Please confirm your signer details so we can prepare the envelope.

Action items:
- Tom: confirm whether FinServe is comfortable with SCCs + UK IDTA addendum as the primary mechanism, and share signer/email for DocuSign.
- Markus/Marissa: confirm we can get legal sign-off and prepare the envelope by Monday 11/16 so FinServe can sign by EoM.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_dpa_redlines_20261113.docx (track changes), SCCs-UK-IDTA-summary.pdf
From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@finserve.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Kaplan <alice.legal@finserve.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA redlines and transfer mechanism preference

Laura — thanks for the thoughtful response. FinServe is OK to proceed with SCCs + UK IDTA addendum provided two clarifications:
1) Data export transparency: we need a signed schedule (or annex) that lists current subprocessors and their locations at signing, with an explicit commit to notify us of changes (30-day notice).
2) Limited remedy language: we prefer a clause that addresses supervisory authority cooperation for cross-border matters — not to expand liability but to confirm cooperation.

Signer details for DocuSign:
- Tom Reeves (tom.reeves@finserve.com) — primary signer (Legal Ops)
- Alice Kaplan (alice.legal@finserve.com) — secondary (Legal Counsel)

If Redwood can include the subprocessor schedule and the supervisory cooperation note in the single envelope, FinServe will review the DocuSign envelope and we expect to sign within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Tom
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@finserve.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA redlines and transfer mechanism preference — DocuSign envelope prepared

Tom — thanks, all covered. Laura and Neha finalized the redlines and included:
- Annex A: current subprocessor schedule (exported list attached).
- Annex B: UK IDTA addendum.
- Clause 12.3: cooperation with supervisory authorities limited to factual assistance and legal process (non-substantive, not adding remedies).

DocuSign envelope prepared and sent to the two signers you provided. Envelope link: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/67890 (attached as DocuSign-envelope-67890.html).

Attachments included in envelope: redwood_dpa_redlines_20261113.docx, SCCs-UK-IDTA-summary.pdf, AnnexA-subprocessors.csv, AnnexB-UK-IDTA.pdf

We will monitor signature status and will flag any comments within the envelope. If FinServe signs within 48 hours as indicated, we will close this deal and proceed with onboarding.

Markus
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Note: For internal tracking, Marissa will update the HubSpot deal (FS-2026-089) with DocuSign link and expected close date 2026-11-17.
